analysis: Examined the two changed files. (1) provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Engine/EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.swift (head lines 80-88): for modelType=="flint" the provider-wide `global` default is no longer consulted. Environment and per-model overrides are still parsed, and any non-native value still throws flintRequiresNative; the function still returns .native. Before the change, a provider-wide global of e.g. balanced would make Flint startup fail. After it, that value is ignored for Flint, so this loosens refusal but does not change the result: Flint always resolves to native live and checkpoint precision. Only the refusal path is narrowed, and the global is a local operator-controlled setting, so no new trust boundary is crossed. The checkpoint-default concern is neutral: the previous code could pass the checkpoint default "balanced" only if a caller supplied it as `global`; now it cannot. This does not alter SSD cache crypto, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, scope salt or the at-rest posture in T-041. Remaining questions: callers of resolve() were not supplied, so I could not check whether any caller passes a global for Flint and relies on the throw. The docs claim that Flint is paged-only and that DARKBLOOM_FLINT_BACKEND may only be unset or paged, which is outside the supplied source (the enforcement is not visible here); this is a documentation change with no security control change. (2) docs/developer/test.md is a documentation-only change with no executable security effect. The test doc text is consistent with the threat-model guidance on isolated keys and cache roots. No regressions identified.
